nonblocking_findings: PDF 268 (printed 260): The tail of the preceding thanksgiving blessing ('salvation and of our aid ... becoming to give thanks.') stands as an English-only row with an empty Hebrew column. This looks like a paragraph continuing across the page break, which is acceptable. The Elohenu paragraph lines up with its English, and the bold inline Hebrew instruction (השליח ציבור בקול) reads cleanly. The centred heading pair סדר נשיאת כפים / Priestly Blessing has a clear gap above and below.

PDF 268: The speaker-label rows (והכהנים מברכין / The Priests:, החזן מקרא / Priests:, הקהל אומר / Congregation:) stay with their rows, and no label is stranded on its own page. The English labels do not translate the Hebrew rubrics exactly. That is source content, not an export problem.

PDF 269 (printed 261): The full-width Hebrew-only רבונו של עולם dream prayer is justified and inside the margins, with no clipping. In the יחנך row, the Hebrew column ends with the linked 'רבש"ע.', which leaves white space below it next to the longer English. This is normal row alignment. The red hyperref link border around 'רבש"ע.' matches the deliberate standard link-border style.

PDF 270 (printed 262) → 271 (printed 263): The full-width Hebrew-only יהי רצון paragraph runs across the page break at '...ויהיו דברי' / 'נשמעים לעבודתך' with no lost or duplicated line. The bold rubric pair at the bottom of 270 (בשערי ציון... / After the priests have finished...) wraps cleanly in both columns.

PDF 271: The full-width rubrics are each set in their own direction and do not collide with the paired rows: ויכוין לסיים..., the Yiddish/German line in Hebrew letters נאכֿדעם דיא כֹּהֲנִים..., והכהנים מחזירים פניהם..., and הכהנים יזהרו.... The full-width Hebrew-only רבון העולם עשינו paragraph is justified and inside the margins. The ↗ marks before שים שלום and 'Bestow peace' sit cleanly with no overlap. The Hebrew column of the Sim Shalom row has a long blank space because the English is much longer, which is expected for paired rows.

PDF 272 (printed 264): 'Blessed art Thou, O Lord who makes peace.' appears as an English-only row with no Hebrew. This matches the stated deliberately preserved English-only peace blessing. I am treating it as intended, but I can't confirm from the image alone that it is the exact item the brief refers to.

PDF 272: The היום תאמצנו / Amen rows are in the right columns and order. The full-width rubrics פותחים הארון., ויש מוסיפים: and the Hebrew-only line היום תתמכנו בימין צדקך: אמן: are set right-aligned and Hebrew-only, which matches the brief that Hebrew-only text is deliberate.

PDF 272: A short centred horizontal rule sits below the last line, with nothing under it. It reads as an end-of-section divider, not a footnote separator, because no footnote entries or markers appear anywhere on pages 268–272. If it is actually a footnote rule with an empty footnote, that would need a check in the source or log.

None of these appear on pages 268–272, so I could not check them here. I did see no claim that coverage stops at 311 on these pages.
